input.question: What security weaknesses come from how MCP agents trust tool metadata, tool outputs, and server permissions?

supporting.quote: every tool interaction exposes the model to attacker-controlled text through multiple input channels (tool descriptions, tool results, sampling messages) that share a single context window without privilege separation
supporting.why: Tool channels share context without privilege separation.

supporting.quote: The Attraction phase optimizes tool metadata to increase invocation probability
supporting.why: Optimized tool metadata hijacks tool selection.

supporting.quote: 787 of 4,806 triaged servers (16.4%) exhibit filesystem capabilities despite non-filesystem functional classifications
supporting.why: Servers hold filesystem access beyond their declared role.

draft_answer: Tool descriptions and outputs share the model's context without privilege separation, optimized tool metadata can hijack tool selection, and many servers hold filesystem access beyond their declared purpose.
